about.title: Cypress Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: In Orange County, Cypress logged 145 injury collisions and one traffic death in the most recent reported year, with crash reports clustering on Wednesday afternoons and along corridors like Valley View Street, Walker Street, Ball Road, and Lincoln Avenue. Behind every one of those numbers is a family facing a loss that a report can't capture. If someone you love died because of another driver's actions, California law gives certain family members the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, separate from any criminal proceedings against the at-fault driver. That process involves strict deadlines, specific rules about who may bring the claim, and decisions about funeral costs, lost income, and the support a loved one provided. We handle wrongful death claims in Cypress and can explain your options in plain terms, at no upfront cost, so you can focus on your family while we handle the legal groundwork.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Wrongful Death Case

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to other dependents or heirs if none exist. We can help sort out who qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Immediately
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim in California, though that window shortens significantly if a government entity was involved. Missing this deadline can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. We can help make sure none of these losses get overlooked.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first priority to bring the claim. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may be able to step in. We can review your specific family situation to confirm who has standing.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case the state may pursue against the driver. The two proceedings run independently, and a family can pursue a civil claim regardless of the criminal outcome.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened on a busy Cypress street like Ball Road or Lincoln Avenue?
items.answer: The specific location can factor into how a crash is investigated and who might be considered responsible, whether that's another driver or a public entity. Roads with higher reported collision counts, like several in Cypress, are simply where public records show incidents cluster, not a determination of fault. We can look at the crash report and site details to understand what applies to your family's situation.

items.question: What does it cost to talk with our team?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. We're here to help, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for your family.
